description: GEER - Marshall Fire, Colorado is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Brad Wham, University of Colorado Boulder (colorado.edu). Reconnaissance of the damage resulting from the Marshall Fire in Boulder County, Colorado. Data included was collected in parallel to GEER reconnaissance mission: 2021 Marshall Wildfire, GEER's first response to wildfire event (report linked below). Imagery collected in 2022 during three general time periods: Late January, mid-February, and late-April. Coverage: Louisville, Colorado | Marshall, Colorado | Superior, Colorado. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Wildfire, wildland-urban-interface, housing damage, water infrastructure. Published 2023-04-25. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
